hero.heading: Hello, I'm Emz 👋
paragraphs: I design, evolve, and make web products more reliable end to end, from product needs through production delivery. Comfortable working in small teams with a high level of ownership, I take responsibility for complete features by combining development, problem-solving, and product and UX sensibility.
I notably designed and shipped a complex multilingual video editor from scratch, covering everything from data architecture to the user interface.
4+ years of experience · Based in France · Remote

caseStudy.label: Product case study
caseStudy.title: Multilingual video editor
caseStudy.actionLabel: View the DRIME case study — Multilingual video editor
caseStudy.intro: An editor designed to turn a single source project into multiple language versions, from preparing sequences to previewing and publishing.

challengePanels.label: PRODUCT CONTEXT
challengePanels.title: The need
challengePanels.text: Producing multiple versions of the same video required coordinating text, subtitles, translations, voice-over and media files. The goal was to bring this workflow together in an understandable interface, without rebuilding each version separately.

challengePanels.label: RESPONSIBILITY
challengePanels.title: My role
challengePanels.text: I defined the architecture and developed the backend and frontend. I designed the editing interactions, connected translation and speech synthesis services, organized file storage and implemented the asynchronous processing required for long-running operations.

caseStudy.workflow: Make a workflow involving multiple languages, media and processing states understandable while keeping the editing experience fluid.
caseStudy.technicalContext: Video projects relied on a complex JSON structure combining sequences, media, timings, subtitles, translations, voice-overs and animations. The editor and player both had to interpret and evolve this same representation consistently.

outcomes.title: Delivered product
outcomes.text: Editor designed, developed and deployed to production.

outcomes.title: One source project
outcomes.text: Multiple language versions without rebuilding each video.

outcomes.title: End to end
outcomes.text: Architecture, interface, background processing, integrations and CI/CD.

caseStudy.conclusion: The editor enabled users to create and publish multilingual videos in minutes from a single source project.
caseStudy.stackSummary: Long-running processing ran in the background, while external services provided translation, speech synthesis and media storage.

overview.title: Product overview
overview.text: DRIME is a responsive, multilingual, interactive, embeddable video player with no cookies, plus an integrated video editor. It relies on a custom .drime JSON-based format that enables playback in multiple languages (subtitles, voiceovers, dynamic designs) from a single video file. This reduces production time, storage costs, and the ecological footprint associated with file storage (one hosted video per project, one DRIME file per project).

caseStudy.intro: Trip&Share | RideShare is a ride-sharing platform prototype initially developed with Rails and ERB views. The project then became a learning ground for progressively introducing React into selected journeys while retaining the Rails backend and part of the Rails frontend.
caseStudy.overviewNote: The prototype includes accounts, profiles, vehicles, trips, geographic search and reviews. The complete booking journey remains to be built.
